post.summary: Submit a list of returns that have zero balance due for e-file extensions
post.description:
BatchEFileExtension allows users to upload up to 300 returns per batch to submit zero balance due extensions. It duplicates the functionality available in Batch Manager - New Job - Electronic Filing - Extensions.

Returns must be all of the same return type per batch submission. Various options are available in the ConfigurationXML including printing, client profile data, and upload options. Device ID and Serial Number need to be included in the submission and are specific to the machine sending the API request.

If you select to do "1040 with amounts", the system will read the extension tax liability override amount in the return and set the payment equal to the liability to result in a $0 amount due extension. It will NOT read the tax liability calculated in the return.

This API operation requires the Advanced Tax Efile licensing, beyond the regular Tax API licensing. Please contact your Sales representative for further information and pricing.

get.summary: Check status of the submitted batch job
get.description:
This API will return the status of various batch jobs that are submitted. You will receive a batch GUID returned from the source job. That GUID is submitted to this API to check the status of the job. Job completion times will vary based on the job type and number of records submitted for the job.

It is recommend to not check batch job status more than every 1-2 mins for short running jobs or every 5-10 mins for longer jobs. Return import and export jobs will complete faster than print jobs. It is recommended to test a few jobs that you intend to submit to determine the best frequency for checking the status.

get.summary: Retrieve the list of tax authorities for a given return.
get.description:
When uploading returns for electronic filing, it is important to know which tax authorities are in a return and qualified for electronic filing. This is the first step in the electronic filing upload process.

This API operation is provided a return ID and type of return to be filed. It will return the available units (tax authorities) and their qualified status. If certain units are disqualified or not available, they cannot be submitted in the next API operation in the series to complete the upload process.

The ExportType can be Return, Extension, or Foreign Bank. Each of these types will have different diagnostics that could need to be cleared in the return to qualify them for electronic filing. Just because one export type is qualified for a specific tax authority unit, it doesn't mean that other export types will be qualified.

This API operation requires the Advanced Tax Efile licensing, beyond the regular Tax API licensing. Please contact your Sales representative for further information and pricing.

post.summary: Upload the return units to E-File System and hold it there for releasing later to taxing authority.
post.description:
To begin the upload and hold process, you will need to know the tax authority units that can be transmitted. You would get these units from the ELFReturnUnits endpoint. Once you know which units qualified for electronic filing, you need to submit the request to upload the file. This is the second step in the overall upload process.

The ExportType can be Return, Extension, or Foreign Bank. Each of these types will have different diagnostics that could need to be cleared in the return to qualify them for electronic filing. Just because one export type is qualified for a specific tax authority unit, it doesn't mean that other export types will be qualified.

As part of the upload and hold process, you will need to also include the DeviceID and DiskDriveSerialNumber of the machine that is making the API call for the upload process. The IP address needs to be the external IP for the machine making the API calls.

After submitting the upload request, you would check the status with the ELFUploadStatus call, using the session GUID provided in the response to the call. If compliance messages are present in the ELFUploadStatus call, those need to be added to a new ELFUploadAndHold call with the compliance message included and answered. There can be multiple compliance messages required to be included, so you may need to loop through the process until no compliance messages appear in the ELFUploadStatus response.

This API operation requires the Advanced Tax Efile licensing, beyond the regular Tax API licensing. Please contact your Sales representative for further information and pricing.

get.summary: Retrieve the status of upload and hold e-file request.
get.description:
Once a return has been submitted for upload and hold, you need to check the status of the job. This is the last step in the upload process. If there are problems with return, it would fail to load into the ELF Status system to be available for release to tax authorities.

This API operation takes the session GUID from the ELFUploadAndHold response and provides the status of the upload request. You may need to make repeated calls while the return is being processed until you get the final success/failure message.

It is recommended to not make more than 1 call per minute per upload return request. The time to complete the upload will be directly proportional to the overall size of the return and number of tax authorities being included in the filing.

If compliance messages are returned in the response, these messages need to be added to the ELFUploadAndHold request with the proper message responses. There can be multiple compliance messages for a single return upload. The process will only return one at a time, so you may need to loop through the ELFUploadAndHold and ELFUploadStatus calls until no compliance messages are received.

This API operation requires the Advanced Tax Efile licensing, beyond the regular Tax API licensing. Please contact your Sales representative for further information and pricing.

get.description:
This API operation provides details for return IDs based on the provided filters. At a minimum, the tax year filter must be provided.

There are additional filters for return type, client ID, and other items that allow users to target specific data for retrieval.

There is also an option to sort the output using the OrderBy parameter. The filter and sorting allows users to mimic most options available in Return Manager when searching for return IDs.

parameters.name: $filter
parameters.description:
**Required**.

 _Example:_ $filter=TaxYear eq 'taxYear'


 Replace `taxYear` with valid value.


 
 _Optional filters_: All except tax year 


 _Example:_ $filter = TaxYear eq 'string' and ClientId eq 'string' 
                     and ReturnStatus eq 'string' and ReturnVersion eq 'int' and Signer eq 'string' 
                     and ReturnGroupName eq 'string' and ReturnType eq 'string' and OfficeName eq 'string' 
                     and BusinessUnitName eq 'string' and ExcludePasswordProtected eq 'bool'
                     and LastModifiedDate eq 'date'
                     and PageIndex eq 'int' and PageSize eq 'int' 



`ClientId` will perform a **'contains'** search such that any `ClientID` containing the supplied `ClientId` string will be included in the return results.  
_e.g._: ```...WHERE ClientId LIKE '%[ClientId]%'```




`ReturnType` can be one of the following: I, P, F, C, S, K, Y, X. 



`LastModifiedDate` should be in ISO format. For example, 2023-12-31. 


It supports the following operation: 


- `eq` for Equals. For example, LastModifiedDate eq '2023-12-31'
- `ne` for Not Equals. For example, LastModifiedDate ne '2023-12-31'
- `gt` for Greater Than. For example, LastModifiedDate gt '2023-12-31'
- `lt` for Less Than. For example, LastModifiedDate lt '2023-12-31'

To filter by date range, use the following operation:
- `ge` for Greater than or Equal to
- `le` for Less than or Equal to

Examples:
- LastModifiedDate ge '2023-12-01' and LastModifiedDate le '2023-12-31' 
- LastModifiedDate le '2024-12-31' and LastModifiedDate ge '2023-12-01' 

Both examples will filter for returns that were last modified on Dec 2023. 



When `PageIndex` is not specified, it will have a default value of 1.  


When `PageSize` is not specified, it will have a default value of 10. The maximum page size is 1,000.

parameters.name: $orderby
parameters.description:
Optional.

_Example:_ $orderby={field}


Replace `{field}` with one of the value below.  When not sepcified, the default value is ReturnClientName.
- TaxYear
- ReturnType
- ReturnClientName
- ReturnGroupName
- OfficeName
- BusinessUnitName
- ReturnStatus
- Signer

post.summary: Submit a list of returns to roll forward
post.description:
The rollforward process is used to create next year returns from prior year returns. Common data, specific settings, and carryforward numbers are transferred from the prior year return into the next year return.

This API operation takes a list of prior year returns and submits then to the batch rollover process. The response body provides a batch GUID that can be sent to the BatchStatus endpoint to track the progress of the submitted job.

You can submit up to 5,000 returns per batch job. All returns in each batch job need to be the same return type and year.

This API operation requires the Advanced Tax Rollforward licensing, beyond the regular Tax API licensing. Please contact your Sales representative for further information and pricing.

post.summary: Submit a split joint return request
post.description:
If you have a Married Filing Joint return, you can split the taxpayer and spouse into separate Married Filing Separate returns. This API provides the same functionality to split the returns that is available within the Tax Prep UI. Please see the Tax help documentation of the feature for more details around how the feature works.

The Spouse return needs a client ID defined where the spouse's information will be created. This client ID can already exist or be created during the API operation.

The ReturnCreationOption is used when the return split has already been done on the same return already. The system needs to know if a different return version needs to be created for the spouse or if the prior split return version would be updated with any new information.

After submitting the request, a job GUID will be returned in the response body. This job GUID is used to check the status of the split process request, via the GET SplitJointReturn operation.
